summary: Ruflo (claude-flow) is a coordination/orchestration CLI (26 commands, MCP tools, hive-mind, swarms) that itself has no autonomous file-editing tool-use loop for a single task — its own agent_execute/callAnthropicMessages path is a single-shot, no-tools text completion, and its sandboxed wasm_agent_* tools operate on a virtual in-memory filesystem, not the real one. The repo's own docs are explicit that "Claude Code Handles ALL EXECUTION" — real file reads/edits/bash happen through the separate @anthropic-ai/claude-code CLI, which Ruflo's own `hive-mind spawn --claude` subcommand shells out to (v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hive-mind.ts, via resolveClaudeLaunchCommand). So the faithful single-task entrypoint is Ruflo's own CLI (built from this source) driving `hive-mind init` then `hive-mind spawn -n 1 --claude --non-interactive --dangerously-skip-permissions -o "$TASK"`, which prints a Hive-Mind coordination prompt and execs `claude -p --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions "<prompt>"` as a child process with stdio inherited. Claude Code is the actual model-calling, file-editing, tool-using loop; it speaks the Anthropic Messages API and honors ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so it is pointed at the proxy. Ruflo's own CLI never calls the model directly in this path — it just builds the prompt and launches the real executor.
dockerfile:
ARG BASE=debian:bookworm-slim
FROM ${BASE}

# Self-contained runtime lives entirely under /opt/harness; never touch the
# base image's own python/node/apt packages beyond what's missing.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      ca-certificates curl git xz-utils debianutils python3 make g++ \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ARG NODE_VERSION=20.18.1
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) node_arch=x64 ;; \
      arm64) node_arch=arm64 ;; \
      *) node_arch=x64 ;; \
    esac; \
    mkdir -p /opt/harness/node; \
    curl -fsSL "https://nodejs.org/dist/v${NODE_VERSION}/node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${node_arch}.tar.xz" -o /tmp/node.tar.xz; \
    tar -xJf /tmp/node.tar.xz -C /opt/harness/node --strip-components=1; \
    rm -f /tmp/node.tar.xz

ENV PATH=/opt/harness/node/bin:/opt/harness/bin:$PATH

# pnpm pinned to match v3/pnpm-lock.yaml's lockfileVersion (6.0 == pnpm 8.x).
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code is the real tool-using, file-editing execution
# engine that Ruflo's own `hive-mind spawn --claude` shells out to (see
# v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hive-mind.ts + runtime/claude-command.ts,
# which locates it via `which claude` on PATH).
RUN npm install -g pnpm@8 @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# Build the harness from its own source — never from a registry-pulled
# substitute. Build context is the repo root.
COPY . /opt/harness/src

# v3/@claude-flow/cli is Ruflo's real 26-command CLI (bin/cli.js -> dist/src/index.js
# after `tsc`). It lives in a SEPARATE pnpm workspace at v3/ (root npm workspaces do
# not include it). pnpm-workspace.yaml matches "@claude-flow/*", which means EVERY
# package directory under v3/@claude-flow/ — including cli-core, swarm, mcp, codex,
# plugin-agent-federation, memory, and neural — is auto-linked from local workspace
# source (confirmed via pnpm-lock.yaml: `@claude-flow/cli-core: link:../cli-core`),
# NOT installed pre-built from the registry as CLAUDE.md's publishing section
# describes for a published tarball. None of these ship a committed dist/, so each
# must be built with its own `tsc` before @claude-flow/cli's build can resolve them.
# cli's tsconfig.json project-references ../shared AND ../swarm (composite build);
# its src/ also imports @claude-flow/cli-core's subpath exports (./types, ./output,
# ./mcp-tools/types, ./mcp-tools/validate-input) and @claude-flow/memory /
# @claude-flow/neural directly. memory depends on security's build output (security
# builds itself automatically via its own package.json "prepare" lifecycle script
# during `pnpm install`, confirmed in the install log); neural depends on memory's
# build output. mcp, codex, and plugin-agent-federation have no cross-workspace
# build-time deps and can build any time before cli. This exact order was verified
# locally: install, then shared, swarm, cli-core, mcp, codex,
# plugin-agent-federation, memory, neural, then cli — `tsc` clean on every step.
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/shared run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/swarm run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/cli-core run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/mcp run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/codex run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/memory run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/neural run build
RUN cd /opt/harness/src/v3 && pnpm --filter @claude-flow/cli run build

# Thin wrapper so `claude-flow` is on PATH without a second global npm install
# (the harness's own dist is run directly from the built source tree).
RUN mkdir -p /opt/harness/bin && \
    printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec /opt/harness/node/bin/node /opt/harness/src/v3/@claude-flow/cli/bin/cli.js "$@"\n' > /opt/harness/bin/claude-flow && \
    chmod +x /opt/harness/bin/claude-flow
run_command:
set -euo pipefail

# --- Claude Code (the real execution engine Ruflo shells out to) talks the
# Anthropic Messages API; point it at the recording proxy. Model name is
# swapped server-side, so any claude-* string is fine locally.
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="proxy"
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="$PROXY_URL"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-5"
export ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-5"

# Skip wizards / update checks / telemetry / interactive prompts (stdin is not a tty).
export CI=true
export IS_SANDBOX=1
export DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1
export DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1
export DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1
export DISABLE_BUG_COMMAND=1
export CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1

mkdir -p /out

# Ruflo's own CLI never calls a model in this path — it only builds the
# Hive-Mind coordination prompt (see v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hive-mind.ts)
# and execs the real `claude` binary as a child process with stdio inherited,
# so this bash process's cwd (the task's working directory) is where Claude
# Code actually reads/writes files.
claude-flow hive-mind init --consensus raft > /out/ruflo-init.log 2>&1 || true

claude-flow hive-mind spawn -n 1 --claude --non-interactive \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions \
  -o "$TASK" 2>&1 | tee /out/ruflo-run.log
notes:
ROOT CAUSE OF THE PREVIOUS FAILURE (verified by actually running the build locally, not guessed): the Dockerfile only built @claude-flow/shared before @claude-flow/cli, but cli's tsconfig.json project-references BOTH ../shared and ../swarm, and cli's src/ also directly imports @claude-flow/cli-core (subpath exports ./types, ./output, ./mcp-tools/types, ./mcp-tools/validate-input, ./mcp-tools/memory-defs, ./mcp-tools/hooks-defs), @claude-flow/memory, and @claude-flow/neural. v3/pnpm-workspace.yaml's package pattern is "@claude-flow/*", which covers EVERY directory under v3/@claude-flow/ — so pnpm resolves cli-core/swarm/memory/neural/mcp/codex/plugin-agent-federation as local workspace links (`link:../cli-core` etc. in pnpm-lock.yaml), not as pre-built registry tarballs the way CLAUDE.md's publishing section describes for the shipped npm packages. None of these seven packages have a committed dist/, so `tsc` failed on @claude-flow/cli with ~100 TS2305/TS2307 errors ("has no exported member", "Cannot find module '@claude-flow/memory'", etc.) because their dist output plain didn't exist yet.

Fix applied and verified end-to-end locally in this exact repo checkout: after `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` in v3/, build in this order — shared, swarm, cli-core, mcp, codex, plugin-agent-federation, memory, neural, then cli. Each `pnpm --filter <pkg> run build` (`tsc`) exited 0, and the final `@claude-flow/cli` build also exited 0 with zero errors. @claude-flow/security needs no explicit build step — it builds itself via its own package.json "prepare" lifecycle script during `pnpm install` (confirmed in the install log). memory depends on security's dist; neural depends on memory's dist — hence memory before neural. cli-core, swarm, mcp, codex, and plugin-agent-federation have no cross-workspace build-time dependencies of their own and can build any time before cli.

Post-fix smoke-tested locally (not guessed):
- `node bin/cli.js --version` → "ruflo v3.44.0"
- `node bin/cli.js --help` → works
- `node bin/cli.js hive-mind init --consensus raft` → initializes cleanly
- `node bin/cli.js hive-mind spawn -n 1 --claude --non-interactive --dangerously-skip-permissions --dry-run -o "test task"` → builds the Hive-Mind coordination prompt and reaches the "would execute Claude Code" dry-run branch with no missing-module errors, confirming the runtime import graph (not just the `tsc` compile) is intact all the way to the point where it would exec the real `claude` binary.

Everything else in the previous recipe's architecture and run_command was already correct and is unchanged: `hive-mind spawn --claude` is still the one first-class, non-interactive, real-file-editing path in this codebase (it shells out to @anthropic-ai/claude-code via resolveClaudeLaunchCommand + child_process.spawn with stdio:'inherit'), and its flag handling (`--non-interactive` → `-p --output-format stream-json --verbose`; `--dangerously-skip-permissions` → passed through verbatim) was re-read from src/commands/hive-mind.ts and matches this run_command exactly.

Remaining risks to flag (unchanged from before): this build is large (9 sequential tsc builds across 8 alpha-pinned workspace packages plus the main CLI) and slow; a future dependency bump in this repo could reintroduce similar drift if a new package gets added under v3/@claude-flow/ without a corresponding build step, since pnpm's workspace-linking is silent about it (no error, just an unbuilt package resolving to nothing until something tries to import it). `hive-mind spawn --claude` still warns (non-fatal) if no .mcp.json is found — intentionally not addressed since it's not required for Claude Code's native file tools. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is passed explicitly even though the subcommand defaults it to true, for robustness against future default changes. Ruflo writes its own session/prompt file to `.hive-mind/sessions/` under the task's cwd (relative, not `/out/`) — that's the harness's own unmodified choice; stdout/stderr of the whole run is additionally teed to `/out/ruflo-run.log`.
